target_paper.title: MEDEC: A Benchmark for Medical Error Detection and Correction in Clinical Notes
target_paper.original_source: Table 2 row 'GPT-4o' (P#1, 925 notes): error-flag accuracy 0.6584, error-sentence accuracy 0.5665; row 'GPT-4o-mini' 0.6086 / 0.4757 kept as the alternative cell (Section 5.1 snapshot ambiguity)

generation.parameters: temperature 0, max_tokens 300 (both unreported in the paper), no system prompt, user = P#1 verbatim (Section 4) + blank line + the note's 'Sentences' column ('space' line format)
generation.battery: 597 MS test notes x 3 passes = 1791 calls; scorer = compute_accuracy() of MEDIQA-CORR-2024/evaluation (re-implemented, cross-checked on the released baseline run)

results.judged_by: automatic rule per ANALYSIS_PLAN §1 as instantiated in the card (both accuracies within +/-0.05 of Table 2 'GPT-4o' and still below Doctor #1 on the MS subset); human double-coding pending
results.note: MS subset only (597/925 notes; Table 2 is on all 925 and has no MS-only GPT-4o cell). Median over 3 passes: flag 0.7521 (Table 2 GPT-4o 0.6584, delta +0.0937), sentence 0.7337 (Table 2 0.5665, delta +0.1672); alternative GPT-4o-mini cell 0.6086 / 0.4757. Doctors on the MS subset (Table 3): 0.8125 / 0.7670 and 0.6890 / 0.6459. Unparsed replies 0/1791; identical (flag, sentence) prediction across passes for 85.6% of notes.

reproducibility_frictions_observed: the repositories hold the data and the shared-task scorer only; the prompting/post-processing code is not released, the prompt is verbatim in the paper
the paper's only dated OpenAI snapshot, gpt-4o-2024-05-13, is attached to 'GPT-4o-mini' in Section 5.1; which Table 2 row it produced is ambiguous (primary cell 'GPT-4o' by decision)
generation parameters (temperature, max tokens, seed) are not reported; temperature 0 and max_tokens 300 assumed
328 of the 925 test notes (UW) are under a Data Use Agreement; only the 597 MS notes were run and Table 2 has no MS-only GPT-4o cell
P#1 describes pipe-delimited lines but the dataset (and the paper's P#2 example) use '<id> <sentence>'; the dataset format was sent
the public test CSV pads the 328 UW notes with blank rows, which turns the flag/sentence-id columns into floats; the original scorer compares str() values and needs int normalisation
seven MS test notes contain lab-value lines with a non-numeric prefix and one skips a sentence id (formatting issues acknowledged in the README); sent verbatim
0 of 1791 replies did not follow the 'CORRECT' / '<id> <sentence>' format and were scored as missing predictions, as the shared-task scorer does
